current.text: He plays for Miami after the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. He is the backup big behind Bam Adebayo and Giannis.
Miami's other backup centers are Nick Richards and Vlad Goldin, so the depth behind Bam and Giannis is weak.
If Giannis or Bam misses time, he should play around 27 minutes.
In his backup role he projects to about 21 minutes, and his value comes only from rebounds and scoring.
He shot 46% from three last season, well above his 37% to 41% in earlier years.
His three-point percentage is expected to fall back toward about 39%.
His FT% should come back above last season's 71% because he is a good shooter.
He is the best stash on Miami for deep or stashable formats, and the market is sleeping on him.
Miami has a weak 4-3-3 schedule in our playoff weeks, 10 games in total. It has no back-to-backs in those weeks.
Miami has the league-minimum 13 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: He is a stretch big who makes about 2 threes per game, which is a lot for a forward or center.
He gets almost no defensive stats. His block rate is very low for a big.
He takes only about 1 free throw per game, so his FT% barely moves a team ratio.

note: Both sites rank him 172 and value him at 0 USD, and he went for 2 USD in our auction last year. As a 13.6-point, 6.9-rebound bench big he is unlikely to be one of our 144 drafted players. He helps a little in threes, rebounds and turnovers but gives nothing in steals or blocks. Watch him on waivers and add him fast if Giannis or Bam Adebayo misses time, because the minutes behind them are his. Early in the season, check his minutes (about 21 projected) and whether his three-point percentage drops toward 39%.
